sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Export Distribution of High-Proof Traditional Sorghum Baijiu

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-national tax differentiation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national), supplemented by the special statutory regime for Private Interest Foundations and U.S.-influenced commercial and arbitration practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PRC–Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty / Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (APPRI, signed 7 December 2018)
Panama–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed in 2019; pending ratification status as of pre-incorporation review date)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation regime); Ley 32 de 1927 and Ley 70 de 2017 (legal entity formation); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT Law), Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2015 (AML/CFT implementation), regulation issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); Ley 70 de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo 48 de 2020 (Registro de Propietarios y Beneficiarios Finales — UBO register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Chinese business license (营业执照) of the founding Chinese baijiu manufacturing/exporting company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Municipal Market Supervision Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarial certification followed by Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China; no Panamanian consular legalization needed as both states are Apostille Convention members

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (公司章程) of the founding company, in Chinese with certified Spanish or English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial copy plus Hague Apostille and certified translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport bio-data page of the founder and ultimate beneficial owner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial attestation of passport copy plus Hague Apostille; translation into Spanish where required by the Registro Público

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized Power of Attorney (授权委托书) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and local counsel to incorporate the Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization plus Hague Apostille and Spanish-certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the founding Chinese company, if the company is already registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, ultimate beneficial owners, proposed Foundation Council members, authorized signatories, and any beneficial owner meeting the 25% threshold against Panama's national Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists, UAF and DGAU intelligence bulletins, U.S. OFAC SDN List, U.S. Non-SDN sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU and FATF listings, and Interpol Red Notices. Any hit triggers enhanced due diligence and, if unresolved, refusal of incorporation under Ley 23 de 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro; online filing through the Sede Electrónica / Portal de Servicios Digitales (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal filings and the foundation deed must be drafted in Spanish. A proposed name may include Chinese-script elements only if accompanied by a Spanish/English transliteration and a certified Spanish translation. The Registro Público de Panamá rejects names that are identical, phonetically equivalent, or visually confusing with any existing registered entity, and applies strict doctrine on prohibited/sensitive terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) working days of the written rejection, the applicant must file a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá, attaching the denial notice, a proposed alternative name, and evidence of phonetic and visual distinctness. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a 'recurso de apelación' within five (5) working days before the administrative review body, and thereafter seek judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. Where the rejection is based on a prohibited token, the applicant must obtain the prior ministerial authorization and include it in the appeal dossier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are permissible as the statutory registered office of a Private Interest Foundation only when the registered agent is a duly licensed Panamanian law firm or corporate service provider maintaining a physical office at the declared address. A mail-forwarding virtual office without a resident agent is not permissible. For the commercial activity of alcoholic-beverage wholesale distribution, the municipal Aviso de Operación will require a demonstrable operating address, including storage and distribution facilities; a bare virtual office will not satisfy the commercial license requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 30% to 40% within the first twelve (12) months for the licensed wholesale-liquor premises, driven by municipal and Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) inspections; approximately 5% to 10% for the Private Interest Foundation registered office, rising sharply if the UBO register, AML/CFT filings, or alcohol-tax records indicate non-compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service for the Private Interest Foundation (first year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page translator tariff and market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as implemented by Decreto Ejecutivo No. 25 de 31 de marzo de 1997 and related provisions of the Código de Notariado
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva / Acta de Fundación de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter executed before a Panamanian Notary Public or legalized private instrument)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is codified; the customary declared initial endowment is USD 10,000. No escrow or paid-up deposit requirement applies; endowment may consist of cash, securities, receivables, or other movable/immovable assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], PANAMA. The undersigned Founder and initial Foundation Council, acting under Law No. 25 of 1995, hereby resolve: (1) to ratify the Foundation Charter and Regulations and accept the initial endowment of USD 10,000; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama; (3) to appoint the Foundation Council members and officers, including President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with full powers of administration and disposition; (4) to register the Foundation before the Public Registry of Panama; and (5) to open bank accounts and authorize officers to execute export trade documentation and payment instructions, subject to Council approval for transactions exceeding USD 100,000.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certificación de Nombre (Name Certification Window, in person or via authorized notary/lawyer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed foundation names to the Public Registry to confirm that neither name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Pay the name certification tariff, obtain a favorable name search certificate, and retain the valid name reservation period for the subsequent deed.
required_dossiers: Foundation name request form (Formulario de Certificación de Nombre)
Applicant identification documents (passport or entity credentials)
Sworn power of attorney or letter of representation if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused or reserved for a third party, file a reconsideration letter with the Public Registry Name Section or select and certify the alternate name from the originally submitted list.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá (Panamanian Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución in Spanish, including the Foundation's name, stated endowment, registered office, purpose (wholesale export distribution of alcoholic beverages), Council composition, and Beneficiary provisions. Execute the deed before a Panamanian Notary; if the Founder signs abroad, legalize or apostille the signature and submit a certified Spanish translation. Approve the Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) as a separate private instrument and pass the initial Council resolution, preserving the original for bank and registry use.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter in Spanish
Draft Foundation Regulations (optional but recommended)
Certified KYC/beneficial ownership information of the Founder
Apostilled or legalized copy of foreign identification/signatures
Certified Foundation Council resolutions appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Notary returns a defect or incomplete declaration, correct the deed narrative and re-execute the Escritura through a supplemental act before the same notary, then re-submit for registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registry Tariff and Filing of Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Oficina de Entrada de Documentos (Document Intake Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial copy or legalized private instrument together with the official tariff payment voucher. The registry tariff is assessed on the stated endowment and number of pages; the filing will be inscribed in the Private Interest Foundations Section and assigned a stamping/registration number.
required_dossiers: First authenticated copy (Testimonio) of the Escritura de Constitución
Registry fee bank deposit voucher or fiscal stamp receipt
Duplicate copy for registry marginal notes
Power of attorney of the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of defects (nota de defecto), remedy the stated deficiencies and present the corrective supporting documents within five business days, or request an extension in writing to prevent abandonment of the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Inscription Certificate and Folio Assignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Public Registry signs the inscription order, assigns the Foundation folio number, and issues a certified Certificate of Inscription (Certificado de Inscripción), which is the definitive proof of legal existence for banking, contracting, and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription order file
Proof of full payment of registration fees
Request letter for certified copy/certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For double-entry or typographical errors in the certificate, submit a rectification request and, where necessary, a complementary notarial deed; registry correction is granted upon payment of the fixed amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax ID (RUC) Registration, Municipal Operating License, and Customs Exporter Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Municipio de Panamá (or the respective Municipal Treasury); Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from DGI for the foundation's commercial activity under ISIC 4632; thereafter obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación for wholesale commercial use of the registered office; and register the foundation with ANA as an exporter to enable customs declarations for baijiu export transactions from Panama or the Colon Free Zone, as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Inscription from the Public Registry
Certified Foundation Charter and Regulations
Identity documents of the Foundation Council members and officers
Certified First Board Resolution naming authorized representatives
Lease or title deed evidencing the registered office address
RUC pre-registration form and municipal Aviso de Operación form
ANA exporter registration application and customs sworn statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any inconsistencies in the DGI RUC dossier via the SEDE electronic correction process; municipal refusal may be appealed before the Municipal Tribunal; ANA registration queries may be cured by resubmitting an amended exporter registration with corrected customs authorization forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección de Comercio Exterior, together with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) for export control and the Municipio de Panamá for the municipal wholesale operating license
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Comercio Mayorista (Municipal Wholesale Operating License); Registro de Exportador ante la Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas; and, where alcoholic beverages enter the Panamanian customs territory or transit local premises, Registro Sanitario de Bebidas Alcohólicas issued by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental), generally exempt from a full EIA study for warehousing, office, and export brokerage operations; a full EIA is not required absent bottling, bulk blending, or alcohol storage exceeding the regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater generation is authorized; any domestic sanitary discharges must meet the parameter limits of Decreto Ejecutivo No. 57 de 2000; solid waste, packaging, and empty-container management must conform to Ley No. 7 de 2002; alcohol spill containment and evaporation/VOC exposure limits must comply with DGNTI-COPANIT technical standards and MITRADEL occupational air-quality exposure limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (annual fire-safety certificate); structural load and occupancy inspection certificate for the registered warehouse premises; workplace clearance and occupational health program approval from MITRADEL (Comisión de Salud Ocupacional), including first-aid provisions, emergency evacuation signposting, and spill-response equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama; taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (http://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Private Interest Foundation engaging in Panamanian-source commercial activity must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes). The SOP: (1) appoint a resident legal representative; (2) file the foundation charter (Pacto Fundacional) and by-laws with the Public Registry, legalized and translated into Spanish; (3) execute a notarized application before the DGI using the prescribed SDI-01 form; (4) present identity documents of the founder, officers, and resident agent; (5) provide evidence of the commercial premise (if any); (6) obtain the RUC resolution and certificate. Non-resident entities may also register through a licensed public accountant or legal representative for the sole purpose of compliance with ITBMS export procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime. The PIF is automatically taxed on a territorial basis; income from foreign sources is outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction. No statutory election to be treated as a pass-through entity exists. An entity may elect, however, to be subject to the General Income Tax Law as a 'reported entity' for dual-residence purposes, but this does not constitute a check-the-box election under Panama's domestic tax code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold; all persons performing taxable commercial activities in Panama must register for ITBMS. However, small taxpayers with annual gross income below B/.36,000 may elect the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Simplificado) for administrative purposes, but must still obtain a RUC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI's 'Facturación Electrónica' system. As of the mandatory timeline, all VAT-registered taxpayers must transmit invoices to the DGI using an authorized fiscal transmitter (API endpoint) or the online 'Facturacion en Linea' module within 24 hours of issuance. Each invoice receives a unique tax code and fiscal stamp (digital hash) validated in real time. The system requires XML format, electronic signature, and acceptance of the DGI's electronic clearing protocol before the invoice acquires legal tax effect.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated (0%) under Article 4 of the ITBMS Law, provided the goods physically leave Panama toward a foreign destination within the periods established by the Customs Law. For a Chinese baijiu liquor export wholesale operation, eligibility requires the exporter to hold: (a) a valid RUC; (b) a valid commercial license for alcohol distribution; (c) the buyer's purchase order; and (d) the goods to be exported through an authorized customs office using the pre-export declaration procedure. Services related to export (logistics, freight, insurance) are also zero-rated if properly documented and tied to an offshore destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (original negotiable carrier-issued copy)
Inward Remittance Certificate (medio de pago) proving arrival of foreign currency
Commercial invoice with precise HS code (e.g., 2208.90 for Chinese Baijiu)
Sanitary or phytosanitary certificate for alcohol beverages (when required by destination country)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may perform retrospective audits of export documentation and foreign currency repatriation. If zero-rating is found fraudulent or the export requirements are not met, the exporter is liable for the unpaid ITBMS (typically 7% of the transaction value) plus default interests calculated from the original due date, surcharges of up to 100% of the tax due, and fines under Article 121 of the Tax Procedural Code. Repeated or deliberate fraud can trigger criminal prosecution for tax evasion, with penalties including imprisonment and disqualification from obtaining export licenses. The DGI may also claw back refunds already credited to the taxpayer within 5 years of the audit year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama does not maintain a central bank because the economy is fully dollarized. The SBP, together with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for AML/CFT, is the de facto banking and FX administration authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital and current account convertibility are unrestricted. The US dollar is legal tender and the Balboa is a nominal unit pegged at 1:1, so there are no de jure exchange controls, no centralised FX market, and no prior approval requirements for cross-border payments, dividend distributions, or profit repatriation. The only practical hurdles are bank-level AML/EDD procedures requiring documentary support of the underlying trade or investment purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds Panamanian law. Exporters may retain USD proceeds onshore or offshore, may use them directly for trade settlements, and are not required to surrender receipts to any monetary authority. The only compliance duty is maintaining customs export declarations (DUA) and underlying trade documentation for AML/SBP inspection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. - Panama Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for offshore digital EMIs not licensed in Panama. Panamanian regulatory guidance does not recognize a foreign EMI passporting regime; a non-resident EMI cannot directly access the local clearing system or hold settlement accounts in Panama without a licensed local bank sponsor or authorization as a local regulated payment / fintech company. The practical use of an offshore EMI is limited to facilitating cross-border payments through local correspondent banking, but most SBP-supervised banks reject such structures because they do not replace the requirement of a local regulated bank intermediary. A properly licensed Panamanian payment institution or a local bank's corporate e-banking product is the only fully compliant clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and in-person interview are the default for non-resident PIFs and foundation-type entities. Panamanian banks generally require at least one director, the founder or a record authorized signatory to appear before the compliance officer, especially for capital escrow and trade accounts. Remote onboarding is permitted only where the bank has approved biometric video-KYC plus notarized/Apostilled foundation documentation; even then, the compliance officer must conduct a live telephone/video interview and the bank may impose heightened EDD for any identified nominee or protégé structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Private Interest Foundation chartered for asset protection with a stated active commercial purpose of Chinese baijiu wholesale; underwriter questions the legal compatibility and economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Foundation Deed and Charter governed by Panama Law 25 of 1995 expressly authorizing wholesale export of spirits; certified Foundation Council resolution ratifying the export business plan; commercial premises lease or warehousing evidence; signed international distribution agreements; written Panamanian legal opinion confirming the PIF's capacity to execute commercial contracts; foundation governance and succession documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions and trade-offset screening flags China-based production counterparties plus alcohol-content restrictions in destination jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC-compliant restricted-party screening logs for all counterparties, suppliers and buyers; customs tariff classification (HTS 2208.90 / equivalent) and export licenses; Panama customs registration and DUA declarations; destination-country import permits and excise tax receipts; corpus of purchase orders, quality inspections, warehouse receipts and shipping instructions showing arms-length commercial trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: complex beneficial ownership structure involving foundation nominees, Chinese private investors, and indirect capital subscriptions obscures control or source-of-funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership register filed under Panama Law 254 of 2020; notarial declarations identifying settlor, protector, foundation council, and beneficiaries; audited proof of initial endowment / capital injection showing source of funds; written CDD file retained by the local counsel; Sworn statement authorizing SBP and bank access to the register upon request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: unusual wire and letter-of-credit frequency in the early stage that resembles circular financing or trade-laundering behavior rather than genuine spirits export.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional trade file: signed INCOTERMS 2020 contracts, commercial invoices with exact product descriptions of grain-based baijiu, bills of lading, Panama customs DUA filings, arrival notices from destination ports, and independent verification from quality or quantity surveyors; bank counsel prepares a trade-flows narrative linking each receivable to a specific shipping cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound injections of endowment capital are routed through licensed Panamanian banks using SWIFT MT103 wires from overseas shareholders or foundation sponsors. The field 70 message must clearly identify the foundation name, RUC (taxpayer ID), and a global purpose code, ideally A02 (Direct Investment) under the IMF BPM6 classification, to avoid mischaracterization. China-origin USD/CNH remittances cleared through Hong Kong or New York require the receiving bank to validate the source of funds against the notarized foundation capital subscription schedule; wire amounts above USD100,000 will generally trigger additional EDD and PALA-form reporting. For PIFs, the bank may optionally require opening a separate Capital Escrow Account for endowment inflows and a distinct Operational Trade Account for disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for Chinese baijiu export use two primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier and logistics payments, using trade and transport purpose codes consistent with the underlying transaction; and (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) for large procurement from Chinese distilleries, issued in USD by the Panama bank in accordance with UCP 600. The LC will require a SWIFT MT700 package including commercial invoice, full set of clean bills of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and optionally a quality certificate issued by an independent inspection company. Reimbursement between the issuing bank and the advising bank in China settles via SWIFT MT202/COV. Domestic operating expenses in Panama are cleared through the local ACH / LAFT system and the banks' online wire channels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CNY outright forwards offered by international trading desks of Panamanian licensed banks using offshore CNH, governed by ISDA or long-form FX confirmations
Non-deliverable USD/CNH forwards (NDFs) referencing the CNH fix where CNY access is restricted and an offshore deliverable product is not feasible
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (USD/CNH) available to foundations with substantial cross-border procurement contracts, supported by a standard ISDA master agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Interest Foundation Annual Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) – Foundations Department, through licensed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due within 60 days after the foundation's registration anniversary each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 50 per month or fraction after expiry of the 60-day grace period; continued non-payment beyond 12 months triggers administrative strike-off and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation under Law 70 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Beneficial Ownership Registry Custodian (Custodio del Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; any transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 5,000 to USD 30,000 under Law 70 of 2021; suspension of issuance of good-standing certificates and prohibition of certain corporate acts until regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounting Records Availability Confirmation under Law 52 of 2016
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent as statutory custodian; available for inspection by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Public Registry authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the franchise tax payment and within 30 days after any change in the location of accounting records or the designated accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and confirm accounting records location exposes the foundation to administrative fines up to USD 10,000 and loss of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is compulsory for Private Interest Foundations under Panama's Law 25 of 1995, regardless of balance-sheet size or revenue threshold. An external audit becomes mandatory only if the Foundation Charter or Deed Foundation expressly requires it, or if the tax authorities order a special audit or inspection for tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; alternative use of US GAAP is permitted for privately held entities when agreed in the foundation charter. Simplified recordkeeping is acceptable for foundations not conducting economic activities in Panama.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 70 of 2021 requires every Private Interest Foundation to keep an updated beneficial owner register in custody of the registered agent and file an annual sworn confirmation with the Public Registry through the Beneficial Ownership Custodian. Any transfer of foundation interests, rights, or assets that changes beneficial ownership must be recorded and reported within 30 days of the operation. The annual confirmation is mandatory even when no changes occurred during the preceding year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Beneficial Owners
Register of the Foundation Council Members
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 – USD 1,300 per year, including registered agent fees, handling of franchise tax payment, UBO confirmation, and administrative attendance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary audit fees range between USD 1,500 – USD 3,000 for a passive non-trading PIF, and USD 4,000 – USD 8,000 for an active export-distribution foundation requiring certified statements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial sourcing model: 0% effective CIT on foreign-source baijiu export revenues; optional 2% gross-receipts direct payment for taxpayers with gross income not exceeding B/.1.7 million; PIFs under Law 25/1995 are exempt from CIT so long as they abstain from commercial acts conducted in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 205 (Informe de Rentas) filed through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 (SITR) electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 31 March of the year following the calendar fiscal year; for non-calendar fiscal years, within 3 months of fiscal year-end; a filing extension to 30 June is available upon prepaying 5% of the prior-year tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification (RUC), exact legal name and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete for the Panamanian operating S.A. subsidiary; a non-resident PIF shareholder is not itself a Form 205 filer and enters no figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panamanian sources only.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export invoice value attributable to foreign dispatch and foreign customers is excluded; attach destination bills of lading and LC/SWIFT evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source wholesale distribution income sheltered by the territorial exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report full FOB export sales value here with supporting bills of lading, customs export declarations and bank collection records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source revenues reduced by allowable deductions and 5-year loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure-export S.A., this line is nil; for any Panama-source resale or warehousing margin, taxable income must be positive and arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 25% after deducting monthly advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure foreign-source profits are not included; otherwise a 10% dividend tax is triggered when such profits are later distributed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment interest of 1% per month; surcharge rising from 5% to 25% of the tax due for delays exceeding 4 months; fixed fines of B/.50-B/.10,000; preventive tax liens, embargo of bank accounts and cancellation of RUC for persistent non-filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 930 (Transfer Pricing Declaration) filed via DGI E-Tax 2.0
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due simultaneously with Form 205, i.e. 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers; no independent extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the Chinese distillery affiliate and any regional related importers/distributors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all cross-border related-party transactions, including 53-proof baijiu procurement from the affiliated PRC producer and intercompany trademark royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating margin of the Panamanian distributor on controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use TNMM with a full-cost plus mark-up of 8%-15% typical for third-party distribution; substantiate with comparables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the Local File and Master File are prepared and retained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain Local File in Spanish; Master File in English or Spanish; keep for 5 years; file the Form 930 attestation only.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fine of B/.500-B/.5,000 for non-filing; missing documentation permits the DGI to impute income and apply a 50% surcharge on under-declared taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Franchise Fee - paid by the resident agent through the DGI/TAT digital portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Obligation accrues on 1 January of each calendar year and must be settled before 31 March to maintain good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foundation patent number issued at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident agent enters the PIF registration number and pays B/.300 (US$300) on behalf of the foreign founder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of the foundation's registered office and resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: One sworn declaration covers the PIF and its wholly-owned S.A.; the declaration is not an income tax return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Monthly B/.50 surcharge; loss of good standing; three consecutive years of non-payment allow administrative dissolution of the foundation without judicial process.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% dividend tax imposed on the distributing Panamanian S.A. where dividends are paid from territorially exempt foreign-source profits; profits already subject to 25% CIT give rise to a full credit against the 10% dividend tax; distributions by a PIF to its beneficiaries are not legal 'dividends' and are exempt from Panamanian withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) in the treaty jurisdiction, execute a beneficial-ownership declaration and submit both, with a DTA relief application, to the DGI through the E-Tax 2.0 portal before distribution; reduced rates (0% or 5%) are applied only after DGI acknowledgment; the Panama operating entity remains statutorily liable to withhold the 10% if the beneficiary PIF cannot evidence residency and substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory WHT on Panama-source trademark/licence fees paid to non-residents (may be reduced to 5% or 10% under Mexico, Singapore, South Korea and UAE DTAs); royalties for a baijiu brand licence exploited wholly outside Panama are foreign-source and exempt. Interest: 0% WHT on cross-border export-financing loans and letters of credit where the borrowed capital is deployed abroad; interest funding Panamanian operations may be treated as Panama-source and subjected to applicable tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama Balboa (B/.) pegged 1:1 to the US Dollar; taxpayers with gross income above B/.2.0 million in the preceding year must file Form 930 and maintain a Local File; a Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds B/.20 million; related-party transactions below B/.200,000 per counterparty are subject to simplified documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply (Law 128/2020, as amended by Law 274/2021): the Panamanian operating S.A. engaged in 'distribution and supply chain management' of Chinese baijiu must demonstrate Panamanian board management, local premises, adequate employees and proportionate expenditure, and must file the annual economic substance affirmation with the DGI by 30 April; a pure-equity-holding PIF qualifies for the simplified low-substance regime and files a sworn statement without meeting full ESR substance tests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a nil Form 205 while export purchase contracts and sales proceeds flow through the Panamanian S.A.; intentionally misallocating shipping origin to classify active distribution income as foreign-source; fabricating deductible commissions payable to the Chinese affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 70 of 2019, tax evasion carries fines of up to 5 times the evaded tax and imprisonment of 2 to 10 years; the DGI additionally demands full restitution of tax, 50% surcharge and 1% monthly moratory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives and the PIF Protector are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and withheld dividend tax; courts may impose preventive embargoes, travel bans and disqualification from serving as resident agents, with imprisonment for willful fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF and its S.A. as letterbox entities for global baijiu distribution with no local office, no employees, no bank account in Panama and no substantive board decisions; conducting commercial acts in Panama through the PIF itself, which is ultra vires under Law 25/1995.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR non-compliance fines of B/.10,000 to B/.1,000,000; cancellation of RUC and foundation patent; automatic denial of treaty benefits; the foundation may be judicially liquidated and its assets returned to the founder's estate in a forfeiture proceeding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation's founder, council members and Protector are personally liable for ultra vires commercial debts; the corporate veil is pierced where the PIF was organized to conceal the active business, exposing members to civil restitution and criminal sanctions for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of the ultimate beneficial owner of the baijiu export profits from the Registry of Beneficial Owners; fragmenting LC and SWIFT proceeds through shell accounts in multiple jurisdictions; accepting cash or third-party payments for liquor deliveries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Law 23 of 2015 attracts fines from B/.100,000 to B/.2,000,000 and suspension or cancellation of the foundation's registration; money laundering under Article 254 of the Criminal Code is punishable by 5 to 12 years' imprisonment and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The resident agent and foundation council members face criminal indictment for facilitating anonymous ownership; individual directors are subject to travel bans, asset freezes and extradition-eligible charges in the origin market of the funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Transfer Pricing / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing the Panamanian distributor's purchase from the affiliated Chinese producer so that 85%-95% of the global margin is booked in China; excessive intercompany trademark royalty paid to a Hong Kong shell to drain Panama profit; undocumented cost-sharing arrangements with related Latin American resellers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of the transactions at arm's length, adjustment of the 25% CIT base, plus a 50% surcharge on under-declared income and 1% monthly interest; repeat offenses escalate to criminal tax evasion charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false Form 930 declarations are personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties; in aggravated cases, courts impose civil restitution, prohibition on leaving Panamanian territory, and imprisonment of up to 10 years under Law 70 of 2019.
